clauses.construct: Element — the root of every modeling construct; carries identity, an optional name or short name, and ownership.
Elements — the SysML textual construct for every model element: element IDs and alias IDs, names and short names, and the leading kind keyword (7.2.1 overview).

rows.name: Relationship
rows.source: KerML 8.3.2.1.3; SysML v2 Part 1 7.2.3; SysML v2 Part 1 7.3.2

clauses.construct: Relationship — an Element relating a source and a target end; itself an Element, so it can be named, owned and annotated.
Relationships — the SysML textual notation for related elements, owning relationships and the deletion rules they imply.
Dependencies — `dependency from <client> to <supplier>`, a relationship asserting that the client relies on the supplier (7.3.1 overview).
Namespace — an Element that contains members through memberships and exposes them by name; supports name resolution and imports.
Membership — the reified link between a Namespace and a member element, with visibility.
OwningMembership — a Membership that additionally asserts composite ownership of its member.
FeatureMembership — an OwningMembership specialized for a feature: a type owns a feature.
Import — a relationship bringing names from another namespace into scope, public or private.
MembershipImport — an Import of a specific membership from another namespace.
NamespaceImport — an Import of the members of another namespace, recursive where stated (`::**`).
Type — anything that classifies: the abstract supertype of Classifier and Feature, owning features, specializations and multiplicity.
Classifier — a Type that classifies things directly.
Definitions — `<kind> def <name>`: a Classifier declared with a kind keyword, optional `specializes`/`:>` subclassifications, and a namespace body.

rows.name: Feature
rows.source: KerML 8.3.3.3.4; SysML v2 Part 1 7.6.3; SysML v2 Part 1 7.6.4; SysML v2 Part 1 7.6.6

clauses.construct: Feature — a Type that classifies values in the context of another type; has a featuring type and a type, with ordered multiplicity-bounded values.
Usages — `<kind> <name> : <Type>`: a Feature declared with a kind keyword, a type and an optional body, the reuse pattern of every SysML usage.
Reference usages — a usage declared with no kind keyword (or `ref`), referential by definition.
Feature chains — a dotted path of usages recording the intermediate features, not just a qualified name.

Specialization — the generalization relationship between types: every instance of the specific type is also an instance of the general type (Subsetting, Redefinition and FeatureTyping are its specializations).
Subclassification — a Specialization between classifiers (textual `:>` or `specializes`).
FeatureTyping — relates a Feature to the Type that types it (textual `:`).
Subsetting — a Specialization between features: one feature's values are a subset of another's (textual `:>`).
Redefinition — a Subsetting that replaces an inherited feature, keeping its value set but changing name, type, multiplicity or value (textual `:>>`).
Conjugation — produces a conjugated type with input and output directions reversed (textual `~`).
Multiplicity — a bound on a feature's value count.
MultiplicityRange — the lower and upper bound of a multiplicity (textual `[lo..hi]`, `[n]`, `[*]`).
Class — a Classifier whose instances are identity-bearing objects.
Structure — a Class whose instances are composite structures.
DataType — a Classifier whose instances are pure data values.
Association — a Classifier that is also a Relationship: it relates two or more types (its association ends) and can have instances that are the links.
Connector — a feature whose values are links between its ends; the basis of connections and interfaces.
Behavior — a Class that classifies performances.
Step — a Feature that is a usage of a Behavior.
Function — a Behavior with a result parameter: a value-returning behavior.

Expression — a Step that is computable; its subtypes (8.3.4.8.1–18) include literal, operator, invocation, feature-reference, constructor and collect expressions, the basis of calc and constraint bodies.
Succession — a Connector that orders its ends in time (control flow).
Flow (ItemFlow) — a Step that transfers values or items from one feature to another (object flow); SuccessionFlow (8.3.4.9.6) orders them in time.
Flow definitions and usages — `flow def`, and `flow`/`message`/`succession flow` usages; messages declare their payload with `of`.
Package — a Namespace that owns its members as a library or model package.
Metaclass — a Structure that classifies metadata features.
MetadataFeature — a feature that is a metadata instance of a Metaclass.
Annotation — the reified relationship applying an annotating element to its annotated element.
Annotations — the SysML notation attaching a comment, documentation or textual representation to one or more model elements.
Comment — an annotating element carrying body text for a model element.
Comments — `comment <name> /* … */`, a comment that may be named and is a member of its namespace.
Documentation — a Comment whose body is the documentation of its annotated element.
Documentation — `doc /* … */`, a comment that documents its single owning element.
TextualRepresentation — an annotating element carrying a textual rendering of its annotated element in a stated language.
TextualRepresentation — a textual body in a named language (the `rep` notation) rendered as an annotation of its element.

rows.name: Packages & imports
rows.source: SysML v2 Part 1 7.5; SysML v2 Part 1 7.5.3
rows.note: used by 637 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: read (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/packages-imports.sysml): `Use::SizeLimit::«ConstraintUsage»` reads `a.w.size <= a.limit`, satisfied on the check, numeric, literal and SMT surfaces; `Widget` resolves only through `import Base::*`, so the import is on the read path

clauses.construct: Namespaces and packages: package definitions and usages, owned members and aliases (7.5.1–7.5.2).
Imports — public/private, membership and namespace (recursive `::**`) imports, with import filtering (7.5.4).

rows.name: Parts & attributes
rows.source: SysML v2 Part 1 7.7; SysML v2 Part 1 7.11
rows.note: used by 632 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: read (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/parts-attributes.sysml): `ProbePartsAttributes::MassCeiling::«ConstraintUsage»` reads `v.mass <= 2000.0` through a part-typed usage, satisfied on all four surfaces

clauses.construct: Attributes — attribute definitions (DataTypes) and attribute usages with types and values.
Parts — part definitions and part usages, composite features owned by a definition or usage.

rows.name: Items
rows.note: used by 5 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: read (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/items.sysml): `ProbeItems::FuelCeiling::«ConstraintUsage»` reads `v.fuel.mass <= 5.0` over an item usage, satisfied on all four surfaces

clauses.construct: Items — item definitions and item usages: things that flow or are conserved.

rows.name: Ports & direction
rows.note: used by 101 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: partial (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/ports-direction.sysml): a port usage is a feature, and `ProbePorts::FlowCeiling::«ConstraintUsage»` reads its member value (`e.fuelOut.flowRate <= 15.0`, satisfied on all four surfaces), but the `out` direction is structural and no surface reads it

clauses.construct: Ports — port definitions and usages with direction (`in`/`out`/`inout`) and conjugation (7.12.3).

rows.name: Interfaces & connections
rows.source: SysML v2 Part 1 7.13; SysML v2 Part 1 7.14
rows.note: used by 20 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: partial (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/interfaces-connections.sysml): the source port's member value reaches a row (`a.source.tx.rate <= 10.0`, satisfied on all four surfaces); the `connection` itself files no row — a bare connect is an equality only under `--connections-as-equalities`

clauses.construct: Connections — connection definitions and usages, bindings as usages, feature values and successions as usages (7.13.2–7.13.5).
Interfaces — interface definitions and usages, the port-to-port connection contract.

rows.name: Actions & control nodes
rows.source: SysML v2 Part 1 7.17; SysML v2 Part 1 7.17.3
rows.note: used by 32 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: partial (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/actions-control-nodes.sysml): the action definition's attribute reaches a row (`x.rate <= x.limit`, satisfied on all four surfaces); `first`/`then` control nodes file no row — the model-checking lane owns them

clauses.construct: Actions — action definitions and usages, parameters, succession shorthands and structured control.
Control nodes — fork, join, merge, decision and the initial/final nodes.

rows.name: States & transitions
rows.source: SysML v2 Part 1 7.18; SysML v2 Part 1 7.18.3
rows.note: used by 50 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: partial (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/states-transitions.sysml): a state definition's attribute reaches a row (`v.modes.load <= v.limit`, satisfied on all four surfaces); the transition graph files no row — the model-checking lane owns it

clauses.construct: States — state definitions and usages, entry/do/exit behaviors.
Transition usages — trigger, guard and effect between states.

rows.name: Calculations & constraints
rows.source: SysML v2 Part 1 7.19.2; SysML v2 Part 1 7.20.2; SysML v2 Part 1 7.20.2; SysML v2 Part 1 7.20.3
rows.note: used by 596 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: partial (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/calculations-constraints.sysml): the asserted constraint usage is read over its parameter bound to the design: the check reads `vehicle.mass <= 2000` and reports `Constraint satisfied (MassOk : MassCeiling, with v = vehicle)`, and the numeric surface agrees; the literal and SMT surfaces file no obligation for it, and no `calc` definition or usage is probed

clauses.construct: Calculations — calculation definitions and usages with result expressions.
Constraint definitions and usages — a constraint definition is a Predicate; a constraint usage applies it.
Constraint usages — `constraint c : C { … }`, a Boolean expression with owned parameters.
Assert constraint usages — `assert constraint { … }`, a constraint usage that must hold.

rows.name: Requirements
rows.note: used by 389 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: read (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/requirements.sysml): `ProbeRequirements::massCeiling::«ConstraintUsage»` reads `v.mass <= 2000.0` through the requirement subject, satisfied on all four surfaces

clauses.construct: Requirements — requirement definitions and usages with subject, require and assume, concerns, and satisfy requirement usages (7.21.4).

rows.name: Allocation
rows.note: used by 5 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: partial (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/allocation.sysml): the construct itself reaches no row: `allocate Supply::volts to Load::volts` files no row on any surface; the neighbouring `LoadVolts` is decided at the load's own value (`l.volts >= 20.0`, `3 vs 20`)

clauses.construct: Allocations — allocation definitions and usages, the cross-cutting allocate mapping.

rows.name: Views, viewpoints, rendering
rows.note: used by 0 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: partial (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/views.sysml): the construct itself reaches no row: `view` and `viewpoint` parse (9 elements) and file no decision row on any surface; the GRAPH rows carry the rendering evidence

clauses.construct: Views and viewpoints — view and viewpoint definitions and usages, renderings, compartments and diagrams as view usages (7.26.5).

rows.name: Enumerations
rows.note: used by 0 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: partial (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/enumerations.sysml): the construct itself reaches no row, every surface refuses it: `Mode::on` — the check reports "Could not evaluate: the body names `Mode::on`, which this lane reads only where the feature states an `=` literal", and the literal and SMT engines abstain with the unresolved-name sentence

clauses.construct: Enumerations — enumeration definitions and usages with enumeration literals.

rows.name: Occurrences
rows.note: used by 0 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: partial (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/occurrences.sysml): `Occurrences::DurationLimit::«ConstraintUsage»` reads `t.duration <= t.limit` over an occurrence usage, satisfied on all four surfaces; an attribute read only — lifetime, time slices and snapshots are not read

clauses.construct: Occurrences — occurrence definitions and usages, time slices and snapshots, individual and event occurrences (7.9.3–7.9.5).

rows.name: Metadata
rows.note: used by 58 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts
rows.evidence: partial (probe scripts/todo-dashboard/probes/metadata.sysml): the construct itself reaches no row: the part's own `s.mass <= s.limit` is read, but the `@Safety` metadata usage is an annotation no decision surface reads

clauses.construct: Metadata — metadata definitions and usages, semantic metadata and user-defined keywords (7.27.2–7.27.4).

rows.name: Cases (case, analysis, verification, use case)
rows.source: SysML v2 Part 1 7.22.2; SysML v2 Part 1 7.23.2; SysML v2 Part 1 7.24.2; SysML v2 Part 1 7.25.2
rows.note: used by 25 of 637 corpus models; parse conformance proven by corpus.test.ts; no probe yet: the case, analysis, verification and use-case constructs (7.22-7.25) are not read on any surface; CU-2 probed the 14 original textual rows only

clauses.construct: Case definitions and usages — `case def`/`case`, a calculation-like construct with a subject parameter, actor parameters and an objective.
Analysis case definitions and usages — `analysis def`/`analysis`, a case whose objective concerns its analysis result.
Verification case definitions and usages — `verification def`/`verification`, a case whose result is a pass/fail/inconclusive/error verdict.
Use case definitions and usages — `use case def`/`use case`, a case with external actors and an include-use-case usage (7.25.3).

rows.name: General view / Definition view
rows.note: general-view nodes draw their SysML notation (adornments, derived names, compartments, port symbols)

clauses.construct: General View (gv) — the default compartment for a package; definitions and usages drawn as nodes and edges.

rows.name: Interconnection view / Internal view
rows.note: an interface is drawn port to port, on the ports the parts have through their type

clauses.construct: Interconnection View (iv) — the default compartment for a part: nested parts, their ports and the connections between them.

rows.name: Action Flow view (Activity)
rows.note: every control-node kind draws its prescribed flow symbol

clauses.construct: Action Flow View (afv) — the default compartment for an action: actions, parameters, control nodes and flows.

rows.name: State Transition view
rows.note: the state view renders a StateUsage node and its TransitionUsage is wired between the chosen endpoints

clauses.construct: State Transition View (stv) — the default compartment for a state: states and the transitions between them.

rows.name: Sequence view
rows.note: one lifeline per participant and one message per succession

clauses.construct: Sequence View (sv) — the default compartment for an occurrence: lifelines and time-ordered event occurrences (9.2.20.2.7).

rows.name: Requirement view
rows.note: an edge renders in the requirement view (the palette spec wires a Satisfy)

clauses.construct: Requirement view — the GeneralView filter over requirement definitions/usages and satisfy/derive/refine, drawn by the requirements graphical notation.

rows.name: Case / Analysis view
rows.note: the case view draws its React Flow canvas; the analysis view draws its graph and DSM

clauses.construct: Cases, analysis cases and verification cases — their graphical notation, including subjects, objectives and results.

rows.name: Allocation (matrix)
rows.note: the dedicated allocation matrix table (matrix-view) is visible

clauses.construct: Allocations graphical notation — the allocate mappings, typically rendered as a matrix or table.

rows.name: Package / tree (Browser) view
rows.note: an edge renders in the tree view (containment)

clauses.construct: Browser View (bv) — the ownership/membership hierarchy from an exposed root, rendered as a collapsible tree.

rows.name: Grid view
rows.note: grid cells carry each element's real metaclass, type and value

clauses.construct: Grid View (grv) — exposed elements and relationships arranged in a rectangular grid; Table 34 names no graphical rendering clause for it.

rows.name: Geometry view
rows.note: the geometry view renders a real WebGL canvas and handles clicks

clauses.construct: Geometry View (gev) — a 2D/3D visualization of exposed spatial items; Table 34 names no graphical rendering clause for it.
